redAtBase: npx vitest run canary-katana-freshness (agents/skills) with the three katana scripts reverted to 07256a2c -> Tests 14 failed | 5 passed; the 5 passing are the 4 --max-age-days usage-error rows (an unknown flag already exits 2) and the degraded-run pin. Restored -> 19 passed. Manual repro at base: 85-day-old map, --strict -> '0 deletion(s) captured.' rc=0.
rootCause: areas.loadCriticalAreas parsed the map and dropped its `generated` stamp; verdict-text.abstains had no freshness term, so a map of any age produced exit 0 under --strict.
assumptions: Threshold is exposed as the CLI flag --max-age-days (int, default 30, must be >= 1). katana has no config file, so the flag is the only config surface it already uses; no new config file was invented.
Age is whole days, floored; a map exactly at the limit is fresh and one day past it is stale.
A `generated` more than one day in the future is treated as 'cannot verify freshness'; under a day ahead is clock skew and reads as age 0.
A real alarm still outranks the stale-map abstention (ADR 0009): stale + finding -> exit 1, matching the existing at-stake abstention rule.

No/unparseable `generated` warns and, under --strict, abstains like a stale map (the recommended option). This changed the exit of five existing --strict tests whose hand-written fixtures had no `generated` (proximity suite) or relied on the wall clock (canary-katana.test.ts). Those were incidental fixtures, not a contract that an undated map is fine; they now carry a fresh stamp and a frozen clock, and their assertions are unchanged.
Degraded runs (no map, malformed map) have no freshness to check and are unchanged: still exit 0 under --strict.
The base-ancestor check (option b) was declined and is not implemented.
The clock is injected via main(argv, { now }) (the canary-cry pattern); no --now flag was added.
dogfood.yml runs katana without --critical-areas (degraded), so its exit-3 notice text was left alone.
